clue.text: A scholar disheartened by mediocre grade in foreign language

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the scholar's title goes

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher of the law
C is a middling mark on an A-to-E grading scale

explanation.surface: A scholar is dejected by a middling mark in a language exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the central B out of RABBI, leaving RABI; 'by' just places C beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the tongue of much of North Africa and the Middle East, foreign to an English speaker.

clue.text: Soldiers once more ousting current political leader

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: once more means again
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Troops are back again, throwing out the present political leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' removes I from AGAIN, leaving AGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was a US president, a political leader of the 1980s.

clue.text: Transport worker let in functions in suit

indicators.note: let in means admitted, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a busman is a bus driver or conductor
sines are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: A transport worker is admitted to formal functions wearing a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'functions' looks like social events, but it is the trigonometry sense; 'suit' is slang for an executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is slang for an office executive, someone in corporate business dress.

clue.text: Most happy to have rich cooked dishes, being at end of diet

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of rich are prepared into a new form

parts.note: pies are dishes

indicators.note: at the end of the word diet picks its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful about eating rich cooked dishes at the close of a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns RICH into CHIR; 'at end of' takes T from diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chirpy is a British informal word for cheerful, so its superlative is the most cheerful.

clue.text: Service offered to old people treated for aching joints?

parts.note: Mass is a church service
the aged are old people

explanation.surface: A church service laid on for elderly people, perhaps with treatment for sore joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like care for the elderly but is a church Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rubbed and kneaded is a treatment for aching joints, the question mark flagging the example.

clue.text: Old woman has small scrap for dog

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a tiff is a scrap, a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: An elderly woman has a little fight over her dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Lousy type is mounting protest

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in a down clue the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nit is a louse egg, and also a fool
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rotten character is getting up a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses NIT IS as a whole to give SITIN, read upwards in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest where demonstrators occupy a place and refuse to leave.

clue.text: Trouble as Old Bill's taken over

indicators.note: taken over means placed above, so in a down clue the bill sits on top of the old letter

parts.note: an ad is a bill, a printed advertisement

explanation.surface: There is trouble when the police take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Bill is British slang for the police, but here it splits into Old and Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: English partygoer who makes an impression?

parts.note: a raver is someone who goes to raves, wild parties

explanation.surface: An English partygoer who leaves a lasting impression on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes an impression' sounds like social charm, but it means cutting marks into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who incises designs into metal or wood literally makes an impression in the material.

clue.text: Go on irritatingly about mistakes in salary details

indicators.note: about means turned round, so that piece is read backwards

parts.note: to yap is to talk on and on annoyingly
slips are mistakes

explanation.surface: Someone nags endlessly about errors in pay documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses YAP to PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A document given to an employee itemising wages and deductions each pay period.

clue.text: Depression makes you unwell after very little time

indicators.note: after places the word for unwell behind the letter for time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, a tiny part of the word
rough means ill or out of sorts

explanation.surface: Feeling low leaves you poorly in no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a hollow or low point, like a depression in ground or in weather.

clue.text: Milk about to be brought round — that will please puss

indicators.note: brought round means turned back, so both pieces together are read in reverse

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Milk about to be delivered on the round, which the cat will enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be brought round' reverses PINTA plus C as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint is a plant whose scent excites and delights cats.

clue.text: Dinner manages to inhibit appetite

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold in, so the run of letters sits held within the words

explanation.surface: A big dinner manages to curb one's hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner man is a jocular term for the stomach and its hunger, one's appetite.

clue.text: Cold fool served up in part of Yorkshire as dessert

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces inside the Yorkshire division

parts.note: a Riding was one of the three historic divisions of Yorkshire
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means written upwards, so that piece is reversed

parts.note: a dupe is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A chilled fool is offered as pudding in a Yorkshire district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' looks like the fruit dessert but is a dupe; 'served up' turns DUPE into EPUD. Yorkshire's Ridings were its old administrative divisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice pudding is a sweet milky baked or stewed rice dish served as a dessert.

clue.text: Does she strain herself, loading food at front of supermarket?

definitions.text: Does she strain herself, loading food at front of supermarket?

indicators.note: loading means taking on board, so the other pieces go inside
strain suggests the letters of herself are wrenched out of shape
front of picks the opening letter of supermarket

parts.note: tack is slang for food, as in hard tack

explanation.surface: A question about whether a woman overexerts herself while loading groceries at the store.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of herself splits to wrap round the supermarket letter and food, and the whole clue also pictures the job itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A supermarket worker who fills shelves with stock, which may mean heavy lifting.

clue.text: Send out prepared into examinations —— after these?

definitions.text: Send out prepared into examinations —— after these?

indicators.note: into puts the reworked letters inside the word for examinations

parts.note: trials are tests or examinations

indicators.note: prepared means made ready in a new form, so the letters of out are rearranged

explanation.surface: Students are sent into their exams well prepared after these teaching sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' shuffles the three letters of out before 'into' places them; the whole clue pictures teaching sessions that come before exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorials are teaching sessions that ready students so they go into exams prepared.

clue.text: Lido's open — endless splashing here?

indicators.note: splashing suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order
endless means without its last letter, so the final letter of open is dropped

explanation.surface: The lido is open, so swimmers splash about by the water all day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts open to OPE; 'splashing' rearranges LIDOS plus OPE. The whole clue pictures the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The area around a swimming pool, where splashing goes on at an open lido.

clue.text: Dull fellow wearing jumper and tee-shirt, perhaps, for work

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the outer pieces go round the inner ones

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a jumper
a tee-shirt is an example of a top
matt means dull, not glossy
he is a fellow, a male person

explanation.surface: A boring man in a sweater and T-shirt arrives for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater but is a kangaroo. Room at the Top is a novel by John Braine.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of John Braine's 1957 novel, a literary work, later filmed.

clue.text: Harness horse, longing to get in the saddle

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
an itch is a longing
up means riding, mounted on a horse

explanation.surface: Someone eager to ride harnesses a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' seems to be the animal being harnessed but is slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch up is to fasten an animal to a cart or plough, to put it in harness.

clue.text: Sample egg taken from cooker in kitchen?

indicators.note: taken from means removed out of the appliance word

parts.note: a toaster is a kitchen appliance that cooks bread
an egg is O-shaped, so O

explanation.surface: A trial portion of egg is lifted from the kitchen stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' removes O from TOASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample of something to try.

clue.text: In part of garden, worker's beginning to prepare container for soil

indicators.note: In at the start puts the worker and the letter inside the garden piece

parts.note: a plot is a patch of garden
an ant is a worker

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of prepare

explanation.surface: In a garden bed, a gardener starts preparing a pot to fill with earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker's' is worker is; 'beginning to' takes P from prepare.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant pot is a container filled with compost or soil to grow plants in.

clue.text: Maybe Times pages contain article about uprising

indicators.note: contain means hold within, so the article goes inside

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means read upwards, so that piece is reversed

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Perhaps The Times will carry an article about a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like a rebellion but reverses RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is an example of a newspaper, hence Maybe.

clue.text: Like Circle Line to be innovative, though short of capital upfront

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: radical means innovative, departing from tradition

indicators.note: upfront picks the opening letter of capital

explanation.surface: A London Underground line described as ground-breaking, though it lacks money to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' drops the C (front of capital) from RADICAL. A circle line here is a radius, not the London Tube line.
explanation.definitionFit: A line from a circle's centre to its edge is a radius, hence radial.

clue.text: Powerful cleric is bound to go by the book

indicators.note: to go by means to sit beside, so the book letter is placed next to the rest

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
a hop is a bound, a small jump

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is obliged to follow the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like obliged but is a jump; 'go by the book' is an idiom for following rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy with authority over a diocese.

clue.text: Female equality originally introduced into personnel department

indicators.note: introduced into means put inside the department's letters

parts.note: HR is human resources, the personnel department

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of equality

explanation.surface: Gender equality was first brought into the staffing office.
explanation.definitionFit: Her is the female object pronoun, used of a woman.

clue.text: Bloomer made by lofty-sounding individual having bible partly closed in a church

indicators.note: sounding signals the spoken form of the word for lofty

parts.note: lofty means high, and the word is said aloud

indicators.note: closed in means shut inside, so the middle pieces go into the outer ones

parts.note: I is a single person, oneself
NT, the New Testament, is part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A gaffe by a self-important person carrying a Bible into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant. HY is said like high.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is literally something that blooms, and a hyacinth is a spring-flowering bulb.

clue.text: Trader smashed work, creating a spot of grief

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters of trader are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A merchant broke a piece of art and was upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' turns TRADER into TEARDR.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of weeping is literally a small spot shed in grief.

clue.text: Backward American lad is so sweet

indicators.note: backward means read in reverse, so the country's letters are turned round

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American
Gary is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A shy American boy is very sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' looks like shy, but reverses US to SU.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugary means very sweet, full of sugar, or cloyingly sentimental.
